text: Bay doors opening. Watch the port side, doc.

title: Watch Ines launch: the port side of the bridge window

text: Capsule away. She is holding position beside us.

title: Watch Ines launch: the port side of the bridge window

text: Doctor, Ines's capsule has lost main power. It is falling.
The recall beam travels at light speed. It must reach her before she crosses the horizon. And Doctor: whatever you see of her left her a while ago.

title: Save Ines: fire the recall beam from the comms console. Wait as long as you dare.

text: Lost main power. Everything's dead except the radio and the backup engine. I'm drifting in.
Don't fire yet! The spectrometer's on battery. This is the best data anyone will ever get.
The recall beam is on the comms console, to the right of the helm.
You should see the ring from here. It's getting bigger.
I can compute the deadline: the beam must leave within 49 seconds of her mayday. The clock is on the comms console. Her picture will not tell you.
Halfway to the edge of the shadow, I think. The data's beautiful.
Doc, the stars behind me are going blue. Is that right?
Still okay. Still waiting. Don't fire yet.
Everything overhead is so bright I can barely read the instruments.
The black fills most of the window now.
Okay. Maybe now, doc?
Doc? Now would be good.
The beam never caught her. By her own clock she had already crossed the horizon and reached the centre.
Fire. Fire now.
I can't tell if you've fired.
It doesn't look like anything. There's no edge.

title: Save Ines: fire the recall beam from the comms console. Wait as long as you dare.

text: The comms console now shows the spacetime map. The red dashed line is the last moment the beam can still reach her.
Doctor, Ines's capsule has lost main power. It is falling.
The recall beam travels at light speed. It must reach her before she crosses the horizon. And Doctor: whatever you see of her left her a while ago.

title: Save Ines: fire the recall beam from the comms console. Wait as long as you dare.

text: Lost main power. Everything's dead except the radio and the backup engine. I'm drifting in.
Don't fire yet! The spectrometer's on battery. This is the best data anyone will ever get.
Beam delivered, in time. But her picture will keep falling for a while, and her older messages are still on their way. That is old light: she is already climbing. Her reply will come after them.

title: Save Ines: fire the recall beam from the comms console. Wait as long as you dare.
Wait for Ines's reply: its light is still on the way (comms console)

text: Engine's lit! I felt that. I'm climbing. I'm coming home!
You fired 43 seconds before the last possible moment. At that moment your screen showed her 9.9 rₛ out, looking almost normal.
Docked. Hands still shaking.

title: Wait for Ines's reply: its light is still on the way (comms console)
Take the Tern down until the relay clock runs twice as fast (helm)

text: You know what scares me? On your screen I looked fine the whole time. If you'd waited until I looked like I was in trouble...
It would have been far too late. By the deadline, her picture was still only a third of the way down.
Relay clock at double speed. Hold here for twenty seconds.

title: Take the Tern down until the relay clock runs twice as fast (helm)
Hold at twice the relay rate for 20 seconds (helm)

text: I want to see that again. Without dying this time.
The window's gone completely black. WREN, is the camera broken?
The station-keeping field can take us lower. Below 1.33 rₛ, every second aboard is two seconds on the relay far away.
No. From this low, the shadow covers more than half the sky. Every star is squeezed into a bright patch behind us. The helm screen shows the rear camera.
Okay. That's enough. Take us back up.

title: Hold at twice the relay rate for 20 seconds (helm)

text: Back at station. The rest of the universe aged 39 seconds more than we did down there.

title: IV · Orpheus
subtitle: The last probe has a camera.

text: One probe left. Orpheus. It has a camera, and it streams.
Orpheus is loaded at the probe console. Its feed will show on the starboard screen.

title: Launch Orpheus (probe console), then watch its feed (starboard screen)
